title: Efficient Digital Root Computation via Modular Arithmetic
description: Formalizes the O(1) digital root formula: digitalRoot(n) = 1 + ((n-1) mod 9) for n > 0. Proves idempotency, divisibility characterizations by 3 and 9, congruence with mod 9, and concrete examples. The closed-form formula avoids iterative digit summation.

overview.historicalContext: The digital root (iterative digit sum) has been used for centuries in 'casting out nines' to check arithmetic. The closed-form formula digitalRoot(n) = 1 + ((n-1) mod 9) reduces this to O(1).
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the efficient O(1) digital root computation and its properties.
overview.text: Formalizes the digital root via modular arithmetic.
keyInsights: The key identity: 10 ≡ 1 (mod 9), so n ≡ digitSum(n) (mod 9)
Iterating digit summation converges to n mod 9 (adjusted for 0/9)
The digital root is idempotent and respects addition/multiplication mod 9
overview.proofStrategy: Formalizes the digital root via modular arithmetic.
